newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial shares nourish on heavy rains.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial shares nourish on heavy rains.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index shot to another record high on Thursday as local investors continued to plough into a market many analysts see flourishing into the new year on heavy rains lashing the southern African country.

"The local investors are excited with the rains...and I think this excitement is going to rub onto the foreign investors (who have been on the sidelines over the week) in coming days," one broker said.
"The rains have boosted the economic outlook," he said of Zimbabwe's agriculture-based economy which many expect to grow by seven percent next year from an estimated five percent in 1996.
"People are getting into the market, buying and holding, and the volumes will soon be running thin," he added.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's main 57-counter industrial index leapt 51.69 points to a record 8,091.61 with gains being recorded across the board, including in heavyweight stocks conglomerate Delta, which rose 45 cents to 3,350, and clothing group Edgars which upped 150 cents to 3,250.
Minings were generally weaker in thin trade.
The seven-counter mining index ended 5.59 points lower at 1,219.75, dragged down by losses in gold giant Ashanti which shed 500 cents to 13,000.
